title: How often does live --wait look for a change?
body:
**Chose:** `--wait` stats `events.jsonl` and `state.json` every 100 ms and rebuilds the snapshot as soon as either changes, and at least once a second otherwise.
**Over:** a plain full reread once a second, as the PRD's "rereads every second" reads literally.
**Because:** with 1 s polls an event appended at 1 s can be seen only at 2 s, which makes "ends a `--wait 5` within 2 s" a race. Two stats per 100 ms cost nothing; the heavy reread stays at most once a second when nothing moved.
**Undo:** set `POLL` to `REREAD` in `src/cli/live.rs`.

title: What does a finished worker's tail show?
body:
**Chose:** a worker that is not alive reads newest-first only down to its `result` line, so its `doing` and `narration` are null when the `result` is its last line, and its `running` is always null. A `STATUS: failed` result gives `outcome.status: null`, because the field lists only `done|blocked`.
**Over:** reading a finished worker's stream to the 1 MiB budget like a live one, so it keeps showing its last tool and a heartbeat that will never clear.
**Because:** the slice says a finished worker "reads only as far as its `result` line", and a dead process has no tool still running. A heartbeat with no `tool_result` after it would otherwise show a killed worker as busy forever.
**Undo:** in `read_tail` (`src/live/workers.rs`), drop the `!alive` stop on the `result` line and the final `running = None`.

title: What does a collect do when its progress sink fails?
body:
**Chose:** a sink error during the passes is returned by `run_passes` once every pass has ended, and the second opinion turns it into `fallback owed — unreviewed: <error>`, so the file is written and a respawn reruns it. A sink error on `Started` before any reviewer spawns is unreviewed the same way; on a size-skipped collect it is `collect`'s error, which the polish driver logs as "collect failed". A collect that fails before `Started` (no HEAD) still emits `collect_done {ok: false}`.
**Over:** propagating the emit error out of `collected()` and stopping the driver, or ignoring sink errors.
**Because:** the collected file's contract is that every failure after the git reads is written into it, and a failed `events.jsonl` write must not cost the reviews' spend silently nor stop polish.
**Undo:** in `src/collect.rs`, `?` the sink calls out of `second_opinion` instead of mapping them to `unreviewed`.

title: Does a CI wait on no running check emit ci_waiting?
body:
**Chose:** `ci_waiting` is emitted only for a non-empty set of running checks. A poll whose set is empty (head lag, no checks in the grace, every pending row a stale rerun row) emits nothing and leaves the dedup alone, so `["test"]`, then a lag, then `["test"]` is one event. Rows whose job link is in the watch's rerun set are left out of `checks`, as `ci::judge` leaves them out.
**Over:** emitting `ci_waiting {checks: []}` whenever the set empties, which reads as "waiting on nothing" while the board is still waiting.
**Because:** the slice says pending reasons that are not checks are not in `checks`, and is silent on an empty set; an empty event carries no check to show.
**Undo:** drop the `!checks.is_empty()` guard before the `CiWaiting` emit in `watch_ci` (`src/closeout.rs`).

title: What shape does an excerpt take in live --json?
body:
**Chose:** `gate.excerpt` and `ci.excerpt` are arrays of `{text, hit}`, one per line in log order; `hit` is false for a context line. Null when the gate is not red or CI is not red, `[]` when red and nothing matched.
**Over:** an array of plain strings.
**Because:** the extractor marks matches apart from context so a title never comes from the line above a failure; the panel needs the same mark to highlight the failing line, and strings would drop it.
**Undo:** map `excerpt_json` in `src/live/gate.rs` to the texts alone.

title: How literally does the extractor read the generic set and the always-add rule?
body:
**Chose:** `affected by [1-9]\d* vulnerabilit` (a green govulncheck prints "affected by 0 vulnerabilities"); the exit rule also matches `make[N]: *** … Error`; the last `=== N.` header is a context line, added only when something else matched, so a green log still gives nothing; tiers are exclusive: project patterns, else structured `failures[]`, else red lines with the generic set; a line rewritten with `\r` keeps its last segment; every excerpt line is cut to 300 chars.
**Over:** `affected by \d+ vulnerabilit` as written, the tier header always added and counted as a match, and CR simply deleted.
**Because:** the literal reading puts a green tier's header and "0 vulnerabilities" into every excerpt, and a header as the first match would become a red gate's block title.
**Undo:** the patterns and the selection in `src/excerpt.rs`.

title: When is ci null, and when does it carry an excerpt?
body:
**Chose:** `ci` is null only when the run has no events and no `ci/<round>.log` (an old layout, which `live_on_an_old_layout_run_is_empty_not_an_error` pins); otherwise `{state: "none", ...}` until a CI event. `ci.excerpt` is set only while the newest CI event is `ci_red`, from the newest log.
**Over:** `{state: "none"}` on every run, or an excerpt kept once the next CI round starts.
**Because:** the old-layout test requires null, and an old round's excerpt shown beside a waiting or green state reads as a current failure.
**Undo:** the early return and the `state == "red"` guard in `ci` in `src/live/gate.rs`.

title: Extend the red-check test or name a new one for the CI log?
body:
**Chose:** a new test `ci_red_writes_the_whole_failure_log` in `tests/closeout.rs`, the same scenario as `a_red_check_gets_one_fix_round_then_green`, asserting `ci/1.log` holds both stub lines, no ESC byte, and is the only file in `ci/`.
**Over:** adding the asserts inside `a_red_check_gets_one_fix_round_then_green`, as the slice's acceptance says.
**Because:** the QA plan's Prove row runs `ci_red_writes_the_whole_failure_log` by name; inside the other test there is nothing by that name to run. Costs one more two-second end-to-end run.
**Undo:** move the asserts back and drop the test.

title: The worker hook refuses a log body heredoc it reads as gh or push
body: A `docs log add … --body-file -` with a heredoc body was refused by the worker hook as a gh/git-push call (the body text seems to trip it); write the body to a scratch file outside the repo and pass `--body-file <path>`.
